questions.question: How is the universe described at the beginning of this passage?
questions.answer: It is pictured as a well-run kingdom or city where everything has an assigned duty and follows it in order.

questions.question: What does the behavior of all things and all species show in that kingdom-like picture?
questions.answer: It shows obedience, order, and organized purpose.

questions.question: What range of created beings is mentioned to show the breadth of Allah’s command?
questions.answer: The passage includes everything from tiny particles and plants to animals and stars.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare created beings to armies?
questions.answer: The comparison highlights discipline, ranks, command, and united action under one authority.

questions.question: What do these many “armies” point to according to the passage?
questions.answer: They point clearly to one complete and universal sovereignty.

questions.question: What central claim is made after establishing absolute sovereignty?
questions.answer: The claim is that no partner can share in that rule.

questions.question: What reason is given from everyday political experience to show why shared rule fails?
questions.answer: When multiple rulers try to control the same domain, conflict and disorder follow.

questions.question: How does the passage use the example of two kings or two local rulers?
questions.answer: It uses them to show that even on a human level divided authority destroys order.

questions.question: What evidence from the world is given against the idea of many divine rulers?
questions.answer: The passage points to the consistent order seen in everything from tiny creatures to the heavenly bodies.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the possibility of another being interfering in Allah’s governing?
questions.answer: It says the order of creation leaves no room for such interference.

questions.question: Besides order, what quality of sovereignty is mentioned as rejecting partnership?
questions.answer: Sovereignty is presented as a matter of dignity and honor that does not accept rivals.

questions.question: How is human struggle for power used as an argument in the passage?
questions.answer: Even weak human beings may act harshly to protect small temporary authority, so absolute divine rule would reject rivals even more.

questions.question: What contrast is made between human power and Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Human authority is weak, limited, and temporary, while Allah’s rule is absolute over all creation.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn about the Lord of all creation and partnership?
questions.answer: The Owner of absolute power will never allow anyone else to share in His sacred rule.

questions.question: What main truth is the passage focusing on?
questions.answer: It is focusing on the truth of sovereignty.

questions.question: How would someone see the cosmos if they looked at it carefully and broadly?
questions.answer: They would see a highly active and flourishing realm governed with wisdom and firmness.

questions.question: What is one sign in the passage that this realm is governed intentionally?
questions.answer: Every being and every group of beings carries out a specific task in an orderly way.

questions.question: Why is the image of soldiers and armies effective in this passage?
questions.answer: It helps show structure, command, obedience, and one ruling authority.

questions.question: Which levels of creation are included in these “armies”?
questions.answer: The image includes the smallest units of matter, living things like plants and animals, and the stars above.

questions.question: What do these levels of creation have in common in the argument?
questions.answer: They all operate under command and in harmony rather than in competition.

questions.question: What truth does this harmony prove?
questions.answer: It proves the reality of one absolute sovereignty and one universal authority.

questions.question: What would happen if many beings tried to direct the same world independently?
questions.answer: The result would be confusion, breakdown, and disorder.

questions.question: How does the passage argue from small examples to the whole universe?
questions.answer: It says that if two rulers cause disorder even in a small area, then many gods would ruin the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: What signs of order are named from both the small and the great parts of creation?
questions.answer: The passage mentions things as small as a fly’s wing and body cells and as vast as stars and planets.

questions.question: What inference should a reader make from that full range of order?
questions.answer: The same unified rule reaches every level of existence.

questions.question: Why would accepting a rival be unfit for sovereignty itself?
questions.answer: Because rule carries dignity, and sharing it with an equal would go against that dignity.

questions.question: How are human beings used as a lesser example in this reasoning?
questions.answer: People, even though needy and weak, often fiercely guard limited authority, showing how strongly rule resists division.

questions.question: What final lesson does the passage teach about shirk in relation to sovereignty?
questions.answer: Shirk is false because Allah’s complete and honored rule over all things cannot be shared.

questions.question: What comparison is used to help readers understand the universe?
questions.answer: The universe is compared to a successful state or city managed with wisdom and strength.

questions.question: In that comparison, what role do created things play?
questions.answer: They act like obedient workers or soldiers carrying out assigned duties.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the commands and laws governing creation?
questions.answer: They are strong, ruling commands that extend throughout all levels of existence.

questions.question: How broad is the reach of these commands according to the passage?
questions.answer: Their reach covers the smallest and the greatest beings in creation.

questions.question: What does such a wide reach suggest about the ruler behind it?
questions.answer: It suggests one all-encompassing authority rather than separate competing powers.

questions.question: What truth is affirmed once this universal rule is recognized?
questions.answer: The truth of absolute sovereignty is affirmed.

questions.question: What opposing idea is rejected immediately after that?
questions.answer: The idea that Allah has partners in rule is rejected.

questions.question: What practical principle is used to explain why multiple rulers cannot govern one domain?
questions.answer: When several independent hands try to run the same work, they spoil the order.

questions.question: How does the example of rulers in one land or district strengthen the point?
questions.answer: It shows that even limited shared rule among humans often leads to chaos.

questions.question: What observation from nature directly challenges the idea of shared divinity?
questions.answer: The world shows consistent order everywhere, not the confusion that divided rule would produce.

questions.question: Why is the mention of both microscopic and cosmic signs important?
questions.answer: It shows that the same order is present in every scale of creation.

questions.question: What moral quality is connected to sovereignty in the passage?
questions.answer: Sovereignty is linked with dignity and does not accept humiliation through rivalry.

questions.question: What does the example of humans fighting over power reveal?
questions.answer: It reveals that even small authority tends to reject sharing, so absolute authority would reject it completely.

questions.question: What does the passage conclude about Allah’s sacred sovereignty?
questions.answer: It belongs to Him alone and cannot be shared by any other being.

questions.question: What is the title of the truth discussed in this passage?
questions.answer: The title is sovereignty.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do we notice when we look carefully at the cosmos?
questions.answer: We notice a deeply organized system full of activity, wisdom, and firm rule.

questions.question: How do the different species appear within that system?
questions.answer: They appear as obedient groups fulfilling particular responsibilities.

questions.question: What literary image helps explain the structure of creation?
questions.answer: The passage uses the image of armies with soldiers and commanders.

questions.question: What does the image of armies teach about the created world?
questions.answer: It teaches that the world works through command, rank, discipline, and unity.

questions.question: Which parts of creation are included in this military-style description?
questions.answer: It includes atoms, plants, animals, and stars.

questions.question: What do all these groups together testify to?
questions.answer: They testify to absolute sovereignty and authority that covers everything.

questions.question: What would be the effect of many beings trying to rule the same heavens and earth?
questions.answer: Corruption and disorder would take over.

questions.question: What human examples are used to make this easier to understand?
questions.answer: The passage uses the examples of two kings in one land and two leaders in one district.

questions.question: What is the opposite of the corruption described in those examples?
questions.answer: The opposite is the clear order actually seen throughout creation.

questions.question: Where does the passage say this order can be seen?
questions.answer: It can be seen from the smallest living details up to the heavenly bodies.

questions.question: Why is this order an argument against partnership with Allah?
questions.answer: Because such complete harmony shows one ruler, not several competing rulers.

questions.question: How does the passage use human weakness to strengthen its argument?
questions.answer: It says even weak people may violently defend tiny pieces of authority, which shows that true sovereignty rejects rivals even more strongly.

questions.question: What final belief should a reader take from this passage?
questions.answer: Allah alone possesses complete rule over creation, so associating partners with Him is impossible and false.

questions.question: What broad picture of the world does the passage present first?
questions.answer: It presents the world as an ordered dominion run with wisdom and strength.

questions.question: How are all beings shown to function within that dominion?
questions.answer: They carry out their own tasks in obedience.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention commands, orders, and laws?
questions.answer: To show that creation operates under governing authority rather than random independence.

questions.question: What is the significance of mentioning both the lowest soldier and the highest commander?
questions.answer: It shows that every rank and level in creation falls under the same authority.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from this universal system of command?
questions.answer: There must be one absolute sovereignty over all.

questions.question: Why does the passage deny that Allah can have partners?
questions.answer: Because shared control would bring conflict and break the order we actually see.

questions.question: What simple cause-and-effect idea supports this argument?
questions.answer: Multiple controlling hands over one task lead to confusion.

questions.question: How does human government serve as an example for this idea?
questions.answer: Even small human communities suffer disorder when rival rulers compete.

questions.question: What real-world evidence in creation is offered instead of confusion?
questions.answer: The evidence is stable order and harmony from tiny life forms to celestial objects.

questions.question: What does that evidence suggest about the source of governance?
questions.answer: It suggests one uninterrupted and undivided rule.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the honor of sovereignty?
questions.answer: It says sovereignty has dignity and does not accept an equal rival.

questions.question: How is the human desire for power portrayed?
questions.answer: It is portrayed as so intense that people may harm even close relatives for temporary control.

questions.question: Why is that human example only a lesser comparison?
questions.answer: Because human rule is weak and short-lived, unlike Allah’s complete and everlasting sovereignty.

questions.question: Based on the whole passage, what is the strongest reason that shirk is rejected here?
questions.answer: It contradicts the universal order, the unity of command, and the dignity of Allah’s sole rule.

questions.question: What truth does this section aim to prove through the order of the cosmos?
questions.answer: It aims to prove Allah’s absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: What two human systems are used to describe the universe?
questions.answer: It is compared to a thriving kingdom and a wisely managed city.

questions.question: What does the obedience of all things suggest about their ruler?
questions.answer: It suggests that their ruler has effective and universal authority.

questions.question: Why are the forces of creation described like organized troops?
questions.answer: To show that they operate under command and are not acting on their own.

questions.question: What is the scope of those forces in the passage?
questions.answer: Their scope stretches from the tiniest created units to the stars.

questions.question: What key doctrine is supported by this complete system of order?
questions.answer: The doctrine that Allah’s rule is one and without partner.

questions.question: According to the passage, what would happen if more than one god ruled the universe?
questions.answer: The universe would fall into corruption and disorder.

questions.question: What common-sense example is given to explain this point?
questions.answer: If several rulers control the same place, organized government collapses.

questions.question: What actual condition of the universe disproves the idea of rival gods?
questions.answer: The actual condition is consistent harmony and order at every level.

questions.question: Which examples show this order on both small and large scales?
questions.answer: The passage points to tiny bodily structures and insects as well as heavenly lights and planetary signs.

questions.question: What does the phrase about no room for intervention mean in context?
questions.answer: It means the perfection of order leaves no opening for a partner to share control.

questions.question: What inner quality of sovereignty makes rivalry unacceptable?
questions.answer: Its dignity makes rivalry unfitting and offensive.

questions.question: How does the passage argue from lesser to greater using human rulers?
questions.answer: If weak humans refuse to share small authority, then the Lord of all power would never share absolute authority.

questions.question: What overall conclusion should an 11th-grade reader reach from this passage?
questions.answer: The harmony of creation and the nature of sovereignty both show that Allah alone rules, so associating partners with Him makes no sense.
